title: Financial Leverage, Credit Risk and Profitability: Does Economic Uncertainty Change the Relationship?
content: Corporate financial performance, financial leverage and credit risk are positively correlated, especially under turbulent economic conditions. Debt finance allows companies to expand their financial capacity as well as benefits from tax shields but increases firms' debt levels and default risks when overleveraged. This proposed research aims to empirically analyse the impact of financial leverage and credit risk on corporate financial performance and to investigate the influence of economic uncertainty on these relationships. The selection of the proposed research involves non-financial companies listed on the NSE and BSE India, uses the quantitative approach, and secondary sources of data through published annual reports, financial data sources and macroeconomic data sources. The observation period is proposed between 2014-2015 and 2023-2024 for the investigation of financial performance of firms under different economic conditions. Business performance is used as a measure of both profitability - profit on assets (ROA) and profit on equity (ROE) - and financial performance is assessed as a set of financial leverage (debt to equity, debt to assets and interest coverage) and credit risk (debt to sales ratio), and economic uncertainty is used as a moderating variable through a specific indicator of uncertainty. Panel regression techniques, namely fixed-effects and random-effects models, are suggested to test the hypothesis. The outcome of this proposed study will contribute to the corporate finance literature and offer significant implications for financial managers, investors, lenders and policy makers.
